procedure.description: intensity modulated radiation therapy planning, left breast after lumpectomy

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for CPT 77301 (intensity modulated radiation therapy planning, left breast after lumpectomy) with date of service 2026-07-25. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Intensity modulated radiation therapy is not medically necessary for breast cancer; three-dimensional conformal radiation therapy is the covered standard.

criteria.text: Adjuvant radiation to the intact breast or chest wall after surgery for invasive breast carcinoma.

A three-dimensional conformal plan was generated and documented to exceed normal-tissue dose constraints (mean heart dose above 4 Gy, or ipsilateral lung V20 above 20 percent), such that intensity modulated planning is required to meet them.
Target volume, dose, and fractionation documented by the treating radiation oncologist.

chart.text: Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 199, LDL 121, HDL 60, triglycerides 114. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
A1c came back 6.4. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 7 years.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end.
Blood pressure check. 143 over 73 today, 131 over 90 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.

Left breast lumpectomy and sentinel node biopsy: 0.9 centimeter grade 2 invasive ductal carcinoma, margins negative, closest 3 millimeters, 0 of 2 sentinel nodes, estrogen receptor positive, HER2 negative.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the fall. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 4 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Patient called about a tick bite on the calf after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

46 year old woman in radiation oncology consultation. Reviewed the role of whole-breast radiation after lumpectomy, hypofractionation, and the left-sided heart question. She is anxious about the heart and asked good questions. Her history otherwise: osteoarthritis of the hands. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Quit smoking 13 years ago, no alcohol, drives for a living. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Status post left lumpectomy for a 0.9 centimeter invasive ductal carcinoma, node negative. Adjuvant whole-breast radiation recommended, then endocrine therapy.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 17 and 19. No ocular pathology noted.
Follow-up to answer questions with her husband. Reviewed the breath-hold technique we will try at simulation. Consent signed. Vitals today 134 over 73, pulse 82.

Simulation. Supine on the breast board, left arm up, deep inspiration breath hold attempted and reproducible to 3 millimeters. CT acquired, isocenter set, skin marks placed. Heart sits close to the chest wall even in breath hold.
Vitamin D came back 20. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Comparative plans, left breast, 42.56 Gy in 16 fractions. Three-dimensional conformal tangents with a heart block: mean heart dose 6.7 Gy, left anterior descending maximum 36 Gy, ipsilateral lung V20 23 percent. The 3D plan fails the heart constraint. Intensity modulated plan: mean heart dose 1.8 Gy, lung V20 13 percent, target coverage 95 percent of the volume at 95 percent of the dose. IMRT required to meet constraints.

Treatment planning note. Prescription: whole left breast 42.56 Gy in 16 fractions of 2.66 Gy, lumpectomy cavity boost 10 Gy in 4 fractions. Target volumes contoured on the simulation scan, plan reviewed and approved today.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
